analysis.title: Asia Open - Macro still rules
key_insights: Nvidia's earnings did not work as a clearing event. SPX fell 0.23% for a fifth straight losing session and closed below its 200-day moving average at $7,346, while NDX rose 0.42% to snap a 4-session losing streak.
Citi's TMT specialist Jon Zauderer says Nvidia could trade range-bound until the CEO succession plan is clear. A report suggests Arm CEO Rene Haas has been approached.

Citi's derivatives desk says Nvidia removed some of the downside tail but was not the clearing event some expected. Jan at-the-money implied vols fell 0.3 vol points in SPX and 0.6 in QQQ and IWM. Clients kept managing hedges actively, with vols implying a 1.33% SPX move and a 2.12% QQQ move around Thursday's Trump-Xi meeting.

Desk flows were net buying of REITs and Utilities and selling of Info Tech, Financials, Consumer Discretionary, Industrials, Healthcare, Comm Services, Energy, Consumer Staples and Materials. Breadth improved after Tuesday's weakness, with SPX advancers and decliners roughly split.

The October FOMC minutes showed a 'couple' of participants thought a hike of more than 25bp in December could be warranted if inflation data proved unfavorable. Governor Waller reiterated his call for a 50bp December hike. The dollar rebounded and EM currencies sold off.

USTs gained on the day despite afternoon weakness after the minutes. 30y yields fell 4bps to 5.40% after a 20y auction that stopped through by 0.1bp at 5.459%, with a bid/cover of 2.63 at the 36th percentile of the past 12 auctions.

Gilts rallied after UK services inflation missed and the BoE projections were weaker. Yields fell 7bps across all tenors and Citi's trader saw better buying in the 5y-10y area. Cable fell nearly 50bps to 1.31, a near one-year low.

MXN fell 2.7%, the worst performer, despite Sheinbaum saying Mexico is 'well advanced toward reaching a deal with the US' on trade. ZAR fell 2% on a 2.7% drop in gold and an in-line October CPI, ahead of tomorrow's SARB decision where the market and Citi's economist expect a hawkish hold.

Gold fell 3.2% to its lowest level in over a year. Copper fell 5%, which Citi's commodity sales desk ties to lingering data center demand worries and a firmer dollar. Citi Commodities Strategy's Nov 6 note warned of modest downside toward $13.3k over 0-3 months.

WTI fell more than 3% to $83 as crude and gasoline stockpiles rose, with crude inventories up 3.38m barrels for a second straight weekly build. Crude recovered slightly after the IDF announced small operations in Hamas-controlled Gaza, which Hamas called a violation of the cease-fire.

Next session: Australia's October labor report (Citi expects employment +35k vs -39.3k prior, unemployment steady at 4.7%), Japan's October national CPI (consensus 2.5% YoY vs 2.1% prior, which Citi says reinforces its December BoJ hike view) and Malaysia's CPI (Citi forecasts 2.0% vs 1.80% prior).
earnings_insights: Nvidia reported earnings of $2.68 on $115.8bn, described as stronger than expected. The note does not state whether the EPS is GAAP or adjusted, or the consensus figure. The stock fell about 3%.
